items.title: Section: Nine Kinds of Resolute Understanding Close Mental Engagement

items.zh: 如是諸相，如前等引地中已說。問：如是作意於所緣境起勝解時，有幾勝解？答：九。何等為九？一、有光淨勝解，二、無光淨勝解，三、遲鈍勝解，四、捷利勝解，五、狹小勝解，六、廣大勝解，七、無量勝解，八、清淨勝解，九、不清淨勝解。
items.en: When mental engagement gives rise to resolute understanding of its object, how many kinds of resolute understanding are there? Answer: nine. Resolute understanding accompanied by inner light; resolute understanding without inner light; dull resolute understanding; sharp resolute understanding; narrow resolute understanding; vast resolute understanding; immeasurable resolute understanding; pure resolute understanding; and impure resolute understanding.

items.zh: 有光淨勝解者，謂於光明相澄心善取，與光明俱所有勝解。無光淨勝解者，謂於光明相不能善取，與闇昧俱所有勝解。遲鈍勝解者，謂鈍根身中所有勝解。捷利勝解者，謂利根身中所有勝解。狹小勝解者，謂狹小信欲俱行勝解，及狹小所緣意解勝解。如是作意狹小故，及所緣狹小故，名狹小勝解。廣大勝解者，謂廣大信欲俱行勝解，及廣大所緣意解勝解。如是作意廣大故，及所緣廣大故，名廣大勝解。無量勝解者，謂無邊無際信欲俱行勝解，及無邊無際所緣意解勝解。如是作意無量故，及所緣無量故，名無量勝解。清淨勝解者，謂已善修、已成滿、已究竟俱行勝解。不清淨勝解者，謂未善修、未成滿、未究竟俱行勝解。

items.title: Section: The Yoga Practitioner's Work Opens

items.zh: 問：修瑜伽者凡有幾種瑜伽所作？
items.en: Question: For one who practices yogic discipline, how many kinds of accomplishment does that practice bring about?

items.title: Section: Four Accomplishments Close the Yoga Practitioner's Work

items.zh: 答：四。何等為四？一、所依滅，二、所依轉，三、遍知所緣，四、愛樂所緣。所依滅及所依轉者，謂勤修習瑜伽作意故，所有麁重俱行所依漸次而滅，所有輕安俱行所依漸次而轉，是名所依滅及所依轉瑜伽所作。遍知所緣及愛樂所緣者，謂或有遍知所緣、愛樂所緣與所依滅轉而為上首；由此遍知所緣、愛樂所緣增上力故，令所依滅及所依轉。或有遍知所緣、愛樂所緣用所依清淨而為上首；由此所依清淨增上力故，令遍知所緣得善清淨，及愛樂所緣得善清淨，於其所作成辦時轉。是名四種修瑜伽者瑜伽所作。
items.en: Answer: four. The cessation of the basis; the transformation of the basis; thorough knowledge of the object; and delight in the object. The cessation and transformation of the basis are: through diligently cultivating yogic mental engagement, the grossness bound up with the physical and mental basis gradually ceases, and the pliancy bound up with that basis gradually arises — this is called the cessation and transformation of the basis as an accomplishment of yogic practice. … In some cases, thorough knowledge and delight in the object take the lead, and through their power, the basis's cessation and transformation come about. In other cases, the purification of the basis itself takes the lead, and through its power, thorough knowledge of the object and delight in the object themselves become well purified. These are the four accomplishments of one who practices yogic discipline.

items.title: Section: How Many Kinds of Yoga Practitioner — Three Named

items.zh: 問：修瑜伽師凡有幾種？答：三。何等為三？一、初修業瑜伽師，二、已習行瑜伽師，三、已度作意瑜伽師。云何初修業瑜伽師？謂有二種初修業者。一、於作意初修業者，二、淨煩惱初修業者。
items.en: Question: How many kinds of yoga practitioner are there? Answer: three. The beginning practitioner; the practitioner who has already practised; and the practitioner who has already passed beyond mental engagement. What is a beginning practitioner? There are two kinds of beginning practitioner: the beginner with respect to mental engagement, and the beginner with respect to purifying affliction.

items.zh: 云何於作意初修業者？謂初修業補特伽羅，安住一緣，勤修作意，乃至未得所修作意，未能觸證心一境性。云何淨煩惱初修業者？謂已證得所修作意，於諸煩惱欲淨其心，發起攝受正勤修習了相作意，名淨煩惱初修業者。云何已習行瑜伽師？謂除了相作意，於餘乃至加行究竟五作意中已善修習。云何已度作意瑜伽師？謂住加行究竟果作意位中，由此超過加行方便所修作意，安住修果，是故說名已度作意。

items.title: Section: A Second Framework Closes the Three Kinds of Practitioner

items.zh: 又始從修習善法欲已去，乃至未起順決擇分善根，於爾所時，名初修業。若已起順決擇分善根，所謂煖、頂、隨順諦忍、世第一法，名已習行。若已證入正性離生，得諦現觀，不由他緣，於佛聖教不為餘緣之所引奪。當於爾時，名度作意。由彼超過他緣作意，住非他緣所有作意，是故名為已度作意。
items.en: Further, from the very first cultivation of the wish for wholesome practice, up until the roots of goodness conducive to penetration have not yet arisen — throughout this entire span, one is called a beginning practitioner. Once the roots of goodness conducive to penetration have arisen — namely warmth, summit, forbearance in according with the truths, and the supreme worldly dharma — one is called a practitioner who has already practised. Once one has entered the true nature that departs from arising, attaining direct insight into the truths, no longer dependent on external conditions, no longer to be drawn away from the Buddha's teaching by any other influence — at that time, one is called a practitioner who has passed beyond mental engagement. Because such a one has gone beyond mental engagement dependent on external conditions, abiding in mental engagement no longer dependent on anything external, this is why they are called one who has passed beyond mental engagement.

items.title: Section: Cultivation of Yogic Practice Opens — Two Kinds

items.zh: 云何瑜伽修？謂有二種。一者、想修，二者、菩提分修。云何想修？謂或修世間道時，於諸下地修過患想。
items.en: What is cultivation of yogic practice? There are two kinds: cultivation through perception, and cultivation through the factors of enlightenment. What is cultivation through perception? It is, when cultivating the mundane path, cultivating the perception of fault regarding each lower level.

blocks.text: Kinds of meditative conviction, what yoga accomplishes, and three stages of practitioner. Two passages (0439a01, 0439b05) are untranslated.

When attention gives rise to resolute understanding (勝解) of its object, it may be: with inner light or without; slow or quick; narrow, vast, or immeasurable; pure or impure. The untranslated definitions (0439a01): "with light" means taking the sign of light clearly; slow and quick follow dull and sharp faculties; narrow, vast, and immeasurable refer both to the faith and aspiration involved and to the scope of the object; pure means fully cultivated and completed.

"The cessation of the basis; the transformation of the basis; thorough knowledge of the object; and delight in the object." "The grossness bound up with the basis gradually ceases, and the pliancy bound up with it gradually arises." Venerable Miào Jìng: the first two are what is produced; the last two, how.

The **beginner**, the one who **has practised**, the one who **has passed beyond attention**. The untranslated prose (0439b05): beginners are either still seeking one-pointedness, or have it and are beginning to purify afflictions; the practised have cultivated the five attentions up to the culmination of application; those who have passed beyond dwell in its fruit.

A second framework: from the first wish for the good until the roots conducive to penetration arise, one is a beginner; with "warmth, summit, forbearance, highest worldly dharma", one has practised; beyond that, one has passed beyond.
Cultivation **through perception** and **through the factors of awakening**.

quiz.q: The first of nine is resolute understanding with inner light. What state does Master Cháng Bǎi describe once the light image is grasped?
options: eyes closed is the same as eyes open
quiz.why: "Resolute understanding accompanied by inner light; resolute understanding without inner light." Master Cháng Bǎi: once the light image is grasped, closing the eyes is the same as having them open.

quiz.q: Where does Venerable Miào Jìng say "pure resolute understanding" extends?
options: both the worldly and the supramundane path
quiz.why: "Pure resolute understanding; and impure resolute understanding." Venerable Miào Jìng: so pure resolute understanding extends to both the worldly path and the supramundane path; attaining form-realm absorption clears desire-realm afflictions — worldly purity.

quiz.q: What are the four accomplishments of yogic practice, and what does Venerable Miào Jìng remind us?
options: cessation of the basis, its transformation, thorough knowledge of the object, delight in the object; if there's an exam, this is a question — remember it
quiz.why: "The cessation of the basis; the transformation of the basis; thorough knowledge of the object; and delight in the object." Venerable Miào Jìng: if this were an exam, it would be a question — remember these four!

quiz.q: How are the four accomplishments related, according to the two masters?
options: Miào Jìng: cessation and transformation are the results, knowledge and delight the causes — and they purify each other in turn; Cháng Bǎi: they mutually strengthen and condition each other
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the cessation and transformation of the basis are what is produced; thorough knowledge and delight in the object are the conditions. Master Cháng Bǎi: thorough knowledge and delight, and cessation and transformation of the basis, mutually reinforce and condition each other.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "transformation" in "transformation of the basis"?
options: 轉 means arising — affliction ceases, and pliancy arises
quiz.why: "The grossness bound up with the basis gradually ceases, and the pliancy bound up with that basis gradually arises." Venerable Miào Jìng: 轉 means "arises" — affliction ceases and pliancy appears.

quiz.q: What are the three kinds of yoga practitioner, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng define the "beginner in purifying affliction"?
options: the beginner, the practised, and the one beyond mental engagement; one who, in access concentration, continues practising to cut afflictions
quiz.why: "The beginning practitioner; the practitioner who has already practised; and the practitioner who has already passed beyond mental engagement." Venerable Miào Jìng: one who, in access concentration, begins anew to practise cutting afflictions is called a beginner in purifying affliction.

quiz.q: In the second framework, which roots conducive to penetration mark the "practised" practitioner, and what do the masters say?
options: warmth, summit, patience, highest worldly dharma; Miào Jìng: outer ordinary is beginner, inner ordinary is practised; Cháng Bǎi cites the Kośa on each
quiz.why: "Once the roots of goodness conducive to penetration have arisen — namely warmth, summit, forbearance in according with the truths, and the supreme worldly dharma — one is called a practitioner who has already practised." Venerable Miào Jìng: the outer ordinary stage is the beginner, the inner ordinary stage the practised. Master Cháng Bǎi cites the Kośa: warmth leads surely to nirvāṇa, summit never cuts the roots of good, patience never falls to the lower realms, and the highest enters the true nature.
